text:
I must give you my hands, wait, still

the earth is full of the murmur of day.

The celestial vault lets none

of its stars be seen... the moon sleeps in the heavens.


I must give you my hands, but wait, for now

everything thinks and works —life is foresighted—

But my heart hides solitary,

disconsolate and sad from the daily bustle.


It is necessary that everything that moves gain

a vague laziness, that effort founder,

that a tranquil rest fall over the world,

an all-sweet, consoling and meek medium.


Wait... sweetly, balsamic with calm,

night will arrive, I will give you my hands,

but now those worldly noises prevent it;

there is too much light, I cannot see your soul.

translation.title: Wait
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the deferred intimacy until night quiets the world.
